OpenAI and others should take notes. Despite making this discovery using an internal model, Anthropic have released a full trace of the two agents that made the breakthrough, including all of the system prompts, user prompts, tool-calls, files, and timestamps. Additionally, Appendix A.7 of Claude's account of the story cites every single outside work that was recalled or downloaded by Claude during the proof search and preparation of the final paper.

This is the standard every single AI company should hold themselves to. This level of transparency is important for mathematicians, AI researchers, and historians to figure out what actually happened.

Also, for those curious, there were three user prompts (presumably after being asked a multiple-choice question by Claude)

I agree this seems to be much more detail than OpenAI's release provided, but it looks like the chain-of-thought is hidden right?

Anthropic claims that this is just how the session file gets exported (i.e. without the extended thinking)

In the exported session file every thinking block is empty apart from an opaque signature field, so no thinking text is available; this is how the session was recorded, not a redaction made for this publication.

The agent was instructed to make notes, and does so frequently in the trace, so hopefully not too much was lost by this omission. In the appendix of "How the one-half result was found," they list the size (in characters) of each of the hidden thinking blocks.
